author: NorthEast News Desk
body: QatarEnergy is negotiating multiyear agreements for U.S. liquefied natural gas through 2031 as it works to replace supply capacity damaged by Iranian attacks, Reuters reported, citing trading and industry sources. The discussions involve major American LNG producers and mark a shift from short-term spot purchases toward longer coverage.

Damage at Qatar’s Ras Laffan facilities has sidelined about 12.8 million metric tons of annual LNG capacity, according to the report, and repairs could take as long as five years. QatarEnergy Trading is seeking roughly 2 million to 3 million metric tons a year from U.S. projects, providing a potentially significant new source of demand for uncontracted American output.

The negotiations matter beyond Qatar because Asian customers receive about 80% of its LNG exports and are also examining alternative supplies. Longer U.S. contracts could help QatarEnergy meet existing commitments while infrastructure is repaired and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains constrained. No completed contract or transaction price was reported, so the talks represent a developing supply strategy rather than a finalized purchase. Their duration nevertheless signals that the company is preparing for disruption that may persist well beyond the current spot market.
dek: The energy company is pursuing multiyear American supply as damaged facilities sideline about 12.8 million metric tons of annual LNG capacity.
headline: QatarEnergy seeks U.S. LNG contracts through 2031
